sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Repair before freezing; all prior instructions remain valid. The attachment-record constraints are not reliably applied to linked attachments: hasFrameAttachment uses sh:node nltl:frameAttachment, but no NodeShape for that node is defined, while the actual record shape targets nltl:frameAttachmentRecord. Constrain each hasFrameAttachment value and each hasSupportingStructureAttachment value as nltl:frameAttachmentRecord (or use a defined shape for the authoritative attachment node), and align the property paths, target class, and supplied ranges consistently. Preserve the existing universal reciprocal effective-attachment checks, longitudinal bracket checks, conditional transverse and side-count checks, bracket-or-similar alternative, bracket stiffening constraints, and universal bracket-thickness comparison.

The frame shape incorrectly places effectiveAttachmentConfirmed directly on the frame, although its authoritative requiredOwner is frameAttachment; enforce it only on each attachment node. Add the declared hasSupportingStructureAttachment relationship owned by supportingStructure and use it to represent attachment to all supporting structures; the current one-way attachment link and minCount 1 do not encode the universal requirement. The longitudinal SPARQL checks only that at least one supporting web frame and one bulkhead exist, not that every applicable supporting structure is bracket-attached. The longitudinalFrame and transverseFrame target shapes do not inherit the general frame shape, so missing attachments can pass; explicitly enforce within-area attachment requirements on those targets. The transverse query also passes when the termination condition is true but no attachment exists. Finally, rewrite the bracket-thickness query as a universal check over every installed bracket (and every relevant frame thickness), because the current FILTER NOT EXISTS is satisfied when any valid bracket/frame pair exists and can let an invalid bracket pass.
